provenance.notes: Executable catalogue derived from the L0 physical contracts. The v1 bridge command envelope remains the only published wire contract; the capabilities below are planned controller-contract v0.1 and require a future controller schema version plus compatibility review before publication through the bridge.

DI.meaning: Binary sensor; polarity declared by implementation.

AI.meaning: Analog sensor; unit and calibration are controller-owned.

SERVO.meaning: Servo command in microseconds or calibrated degrees; local controller owns hard bounds.

MOTOR.meaning: Motor direction plus bounded PWM duty.

STEP.meaning: Stepper trajectory request; never raw remote pulse streaming.

ESTOP.meaning: Normally closed hardwired chain; open or fault means unsafe. Not a normal DI.

LOGICAL.meaning: Logical channel of an orchestrated or structural construct; not raw GPIO.

SERVO|DO.meaning: Composite placeholder for an actuator the L0 contract leaves unresolved between a servo position and a switched enable. The concrete type is TBD-L3 and is not asserted at L1; the composite type contributes to no resolved channel count.

state_model.notes: A command is transition-constrained only when the L0 state diagram declares a command-triggered edge. Commands without a declared edge are controller-owned and are not transition-checked at L1.

admission_contract.position: The admission layer is evaluated before any actuator path is reached. A command that is not admitted must never energise an actuator, engage a servo or move a stepper.
admission_contract.ownership: Local device controllers own motion limits, E-stop authority and every controller-owned range. Admission is a network-side admission filter, not a substitute for a local interlock (ADR-0006).

transition_policies.declared_edge: The capability declares at least one command-triggered edge in mode_transitions. Admission checks the observed module state against the declared source states; ANY matches every state.
transition_policies.always_allowed: The L0 contract accepts the command from any state (for example a local safety stop). Admission does not check the transition; the local controller still applies its own state and fault rules.

error_shape.constraint: the violated constraint, for example range:10..100 or transition:IDLE
error_shape.evidence_level: the evidence level of the schema that produced the decision

admission_contract.staleness_rule: A command whose transition is transition-checked cannot be admitted while the observed module state is unknown or stale; the state is surfaced as UNKNOWN and never inferred (ADR-0006).

modules.name: Brackets
modules.controller_board_note: Structural construct with no independent actuator or controller; the hosted module's controller owns the stop action.

modules.capability_note: No remote actuation is permitted on this module: GET_STATUS is a read-only future monitor (planned v0.1 only, not a v1 bridge command) and is the only declared capability. The structural construct has no physical controller, so the hosted module's controller owns every stop action.

watchdog.behaviour: Not applicable: the structural module has no independent controller.

local_interlocks.estop_authority: hosted module's local interlock; no independent E-stop circuit
rules: No remote command can energize any actuator.

Recovery requires physical inspection plus a hosted controller RESET.

pin_mapping_provenance.verification: Not applicable: no physical controller or channel allocation exists for this construct.

normal_cycle.notes: The normal cycle of a structural construct is the absence of actuation; there is no command to admit.

modules.name: Combine
modules.role: Workflow coordinator across all physical modules

rules: An observed member E_STOP produces SAFETY_HALT.
Combine cannot claim physical stop before member telemetry verifies it.
Orchestration advances only on fresh observed terminal telemetry.
Recovery requires every local controller safely reset and observed at IDLE.

pin_mapping_provenance.verification: Not applicable: logical channels only; no raw GPIO or channel allocation exists for this construct.

normal_cycle.notes: Member staleness, member fault and member E-stop fixtures remain a separate increment.

cross_module_invariants.rule: Network loss, stale commands, twin state, dashboard actions and AI recommendations cannot energize an actuator or release an E-stop.
Different mobile modules require distinct verified controller channels or a formally verified controller-selection interlock; placeholder pin maps are prohibited.
Crane and forklift movement require a local or verified zone-clear protocol; network acknowledgement alone is insufficient.
Orchestration advances only on fresh observed terminal telemetry, never on command dispatch or protocol acknowledgement.
Telemetry of unknown freshness is surfaced as UNKNOWN; a safe or running state is never inferred.
After an E-stop, power or bus loss or controller restart, each module must obtain local safe state and operator clearance before accepting a new motion command.

open_increments: Registry binding of module identifiers to device registry entries (Issue #32) is not part of this schema.
Unity prefab and scene mapping (Issue #33) is not part of this schema.
UNKNOWN and SIMULATED telemetry states (Issue #174 SPEC-5/SPEC-6) are not part of this schema.
The all-module fixture library (jam, missing sensor, limit switch, E-stop, offline, calibration expiry) is a separate increment; this schema carries the NORMAL CYCLE fixture only.
TC-4 measured pinout and tolerances and TC-5 power loss and safety stop require physical HIL evidence and cannot be satisfied by this schema.
